record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
record.original_question: Consider the recurrence z_{n+1} = (alpha + z_n)/(C z_{n-1} + z_{n-2}), for n = 0, 1, ..., with alpha and C in [0, infinity). Is the following trichotomy valid: every positive solution converges to the positive equilibrium if and only if alpha C^2 > 1; every positive solution converges to a not necessarily prime period-six solution if and only if alpha C^2 = 1; and positive unbounded solutions exist if and only if alpha C^2 < 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha, C \in [0, \infty)$ and consider the third-order rational recurrence
$$z_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha + z_n}{C\, z_{n-1} + z_{n-2}}, \qquad n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots,$$
with positive initial conditions $z_{-2}, z_{-1}, z_0 > 0$ (chosen so that the denominators never vanish). A "positive solution" is a sequence $\{z_n\}_{n \ge -2}$ of positive reals satisfying the recurrence. A positive equilibrium is a positive number $\bar z$ with $\bar z = (\alpha + \bar z)/((C+1)\bar z)$. A period-six solution is a solution satisfying $z_{n+6} = z_n$ for all $n$ (not required to have prime period six).

Decide whether the following trichotomy holds:
(i) every positive solution converges to the positive equilibrium if and only if $\alpha C^2 > 1$;
(ii) every positive solution converges to a (not necessarily prime) period-six solution if and only if $\alpha C^2 = 1$;
(iii) there exist unbounded positive solutions if and only if $\alpha C^2 < 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific period-six trichotomy conjecture for the third-order rational recurrence $z_{n+1}=(\alpha+z_n)/(Cz_{n-1}+z_{n-2})$. Related work on rational difference equations and period-six behavior exists, but no direct proof or disproof of the stated trichotomy was located, so its status appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Periodic Behavior in a Class of Second Order Recurrence Relations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses periodic behavior in rational recurrence relations but does not address the specific third-order recurrence in question.
status_evidence.claim: No direct resolution of the stated trichotomy was located in publicly available sources.
